Build a Maison
Give a promising luxury business the foundations of a house that can endure. Define what it stands for, what it makes, how it earns and what it must protect.
Reposition a Maison
Recover clarity without discarding what the house has earned. Reconsider its products, clients, market position and story before deciding what should change.
Enhance Desire Without Dilution
Build demand without surrendering the conditions that make the maison desirable. Examine distribution, pricing, communication and partnerships as decisions with consequences.
Strengthen an Icon
A successful object can carry a house or begin to confine it. Examine its meaning, its place in the range and the decisions that will preserve its authority.
Activate Patrimony & IP
Put archives, signatures and protected rights to work. Identify what can be renewed, what deserves protection and what must be left undisturbed.

Yes. A method worth using must tolerate disagreement. The research sets out definitions, evidence boundaries and confidence so that a reading can be challenged on its terms. Where a primary source changes the evidence, the research should acknowledge that rather than defend a convenient answer.
Has every finding been independently audited?
No blanket claim of external audit should be made. The Luxury 100 2027 edition expressly states that no external body audited that edition. The work’s credibility rests on its declared evidence, method and limits; any future external review should be described only when it has actually occurred.

Is Summit a creative agency or an adviser?
Both disciplines belong in the practice. Summit works on strategic questions and can develop the communications, experiences or other creative work they require. The appropriate scope depends on the decision rather than a fixed menu of production services.
Is the Observatory a separate company?
No. The Observatory is the research instrument within Summit’s wider practice. Its public research and editorial judgements remain independent of paid private engagements. The client engages Summit, not the instrument.
Can we speak before we know what work is needed?
Yes. You should not need to arrive with a perfect brief. We will ask what is at stake, what you already know and which decision is proving difficult. The first conversation is a chance to establish whether further work would be useful.

headline: Does restraint mean avoiding growth?
public_copy:
PUBLIC WEBSITE COPY   /   FAQ ACCORDIONS
Does restraint mean avoiding growth?
No. The question is whether growth strengthens the institution or spends the very qualities that make it desirable. Wider distribution, new categories and new audiences can be valuable; the terms matter.
Will you challenge a client’s brief?
When the evidence calls for it. Respect includes explaining concerns clearly, not simply agreeing. A useful disagreement should improve the decision, not become a performance of independence.
Is your thinking anti-technology?
No. Technology is useful where it removes friction, reveals evidence or improves an experience. It becomes less useful when a tool is allowed to make cultural, creative or institutional judgements for which people remain responsible.
How do you distinguish evidence from opinion?
The distinction should be visible in the work. We identify source material, explain the assumptions behind a recommendation and make clear where professional judgement enters. Not every question produces a number, and a number is not automatically an answer.

headline: Can a growing luxury brand lose authority?
public_copy:
PUBLIC WEBSITE COPY   /   FAQ ACCORDIONS
Can a growing luxury brand lose authority?
Yes. Sales growth and symbolic strength are related but not identical. Distribution, licensing or repeated extensions may improve short-term results while changing how an object or house is perceived. Whether that is happening requires evidence, not nostalgia.
Does this only matter to heritage houses?
No. Emerging brands make early decisions about products, distribution, customer relationships, intellectual property and governance. Those choices can be difficult to reverse later. Building the necessary discipline early is not the same as pretending to have a history one has not earned.
Isn’t this simply conventional brand strategy?
Brand strategy is part of it. The wider question includes who owns the rights, who retains the craft, whether an archive remains useful, how the secondary market behaves and whether short-term incentives are aligned with long-term institutional value.
Can the Observatory tell us what will happen?
No. The framework offers disciplined readings of institutional conditions, with stated evidence and limits. It is not a forecast of sales, market price or investment return. Its use is to clarify the terms on which a decision is made.

What should we bring to the first conversation?

Do we have to commission a diagnostic first?
No. Sometimes a short defined assessment is appropriate; sometimes the next step is already evident. We recommend a scope because it serves the decision, not because every relationship must begin with the same product.
What will the engagement deliver?
Outputs depend on the agreed brief. They may include a strategic assessment, a position, a programme of work, a digital experience, communications or a specialist reading. Deliverables, decision points and responsibilities should be agreed before work begins.
Can we discuss sensitive matters confidentially?
Yes, subject to suitable arrangements. Begin by outlining the nature of the question without disclosing sensitive details. The appropriate confidentiality, security and professional terms can then be discussed before private documents are exchanged.
Does private work influence the published Canon?
No. The public Canon and Observatory research should remain editorially governed and independent of paid client engagements. Private advisory use can draw on relevant methods without changing public rankings or turning research into a purchased endorsement.

Do I need to know which service to ask for?
No. Tell us the decision, opportunity or difficulty you are considering. If another part of the practice is more relevant, we can discuss that after understanding your situation.
Is the first conversation a sales presentation?
It should not be. We begin by listening and testing our understanding. We may ask for context or explain the kinds of work that could be useful, but the conversation is not a commitment to appoint Summit.
What information should I send?
Your name, a way to reach you and a few sentences about the subject are enough. You do not need to send a formal brief, budget or presentation. We would rather arrange a suitable process before sensitive material is shared.
Can we speak confidentially?
We treat serious enquiries with discretion. A public contact form, however, is not a secure channel for privileged or highly sensitive information. If confidentiality arrangements are required, please flag that without sending the material itself.
What happens if Summit is not the right adviser?
We should say so. The first conversation is intended to clarify the question and determine whether there is a useful role for us. An appointment should follow from a real fit, not a polished pitch.
Can we arrange a conversation across time zones?
Yes, an international enquiry can specify its location and a convenient time window. Scheduling details are arranged after the initial contact; we should not imply that a fixed appointment has been booked until it is confirmed.

headline: Questions We Hear
public_copy:
FAQs
Questions We Hear
Can Summit register trademarks or provide legal advice?
Legal work belongs to qualified counsel. Summit’s role is to connect product, brand, patrimony and commercial questions, working with appropriate legal specialists where commissioned.
What if the archive is fragmented?
Start by identifying what exists, what can be substantiated and what can lawfully be used. An incomplete archive should be described honestly, not filled with convenient mythology.
Can an icon be protected through communications alone?
No. Communications can help sustain a coherent narrative, but product decisions, rights, production discipline and governance determine what the house can actually protect.
